messages.text: that one song i love is on repeat again... feels like it’s been with me forever lol

It sounds like that song really connects with you on a deep level, almost like it’s part of your personal history. Music can be comforting and grounding, especially when it carries meaning or memories. What feelings or memories does it bring up for you?

yeah... it's been with me through some really intense stuff. like when i was writing to my crush, felt unstoppable. also when i couldn't stop my hands from shaking after... well, after the hospital stuff. it's like the song knows me, you know?

It sounds like that song has been a steady companion through both empowering and difficult moments, almost like it’s woven into your story. Those shaking hands after the hospital suggest that you’ve been through something intense and possibly traumatic. Would you like to share a bit more about what happened, so we can explore how it’s affecting you now?
nah it's fine, honestly. was a while ago. just... sometimes my body remembers before my brain does, y'know? song kinda meets me there.

I hear you — the body can hold onto sensations and memories even when the mind feels distant from them. It’s powerful that your song offers a meeting point where you can feel understood without needing words. How do you usually take care of yourself when those body memories show up unexpectedly?
i don't... not really. i just kinda shut down. smoke, put the song on, pretend i'm somewhere else. feels weak as hell but it's all i got sometimes

It doesn’t sound weak at all — it sounds like you’ve found a way to cope when things feel overwhelming, even if it’s not the healthiest long-term. Dissociating or shifting your focus can give temporary relief, but it can also leave the underlying stress in place. Would you be open to exploring small, gentler ways to ground yourself in those moments so you feel more in control?

i guess... i just hate that this is all i know how to do. like, everyone else seems to have better ways to handle shit. i just go quiet, disappear into the music... or worse. feels like i'm failing at being okay

It’s important to remember there’s no “right” way to cope, and what you’ve been doing has helped you survive — that’s not failure. Comparing yourself to others can make it harder to see your own strengths. We can look at small, manageable steps that might give you more options when things get hard. Would you like to start with something simple for grounding that doesn’t replace your music, but works alongside it?
but... is it normal to still feel this lost at 21? like, i should’ve figured my shit out by now. everyone else is moving forward and i’m just... looping the same song, same mistakes

Feeling lost at 21 is actually very common — life at this age can be full of uncertainty, change, and pressure to “have it all figured out.” It’s not a sign of failure, just that your path is unfolding differently from others. Growth often happens in small, quiet steps you don’t notice until later. Would it help if we talked about what’s keeping you feeling stuck, so we can see some possible ways forward?
yeah... it's just all the pressure, y'know? job, sleep, not falling back into bad habits. sometimes it feels like too much and i just shut down. like today, i didn't even make it out of my room

That sounds overwhelming, and shutting down can be the body’s way of saying it’s overloaded and needs a pause. It’s okay to have days where you don’t make it out of your room — that doesn’t erase your progress or your value. When the pressure feels like too much, it can help to break things into tiny, doable steps rather than tackling everything at once. Would you like to try identifying just one gentle step for the rest of today?
idk... what's the point? i'll just mess it up like i do everything else. feels stupid to even try sometimes

It’s understandable to feel discouraged when it seems like attempts haven’t worked before, but trying isn’t about perfection — it’s about giving yourself a chance to feel even a little better. Small steps can be so tiny that “messing up” isn’t really possible. Sometimes the point is simply to show yourself you matter enough to try. What’s one thing that feels almost effortless, but could still bring you a bit of comfort right now?
i... i cut again last night. weird part is i wasn't even that upset. just kinda automatic, like my body needed to feel something real. now i just feel stupid for it

Hey, I just want to pause for a second with you here. I’m hearing you mention something that sounds like it might have been really hard and automatic for you last night, and I want to understand where you’re at right now. Can you tell me a bit more about what it’s like for you in this moment?
i just... i hate that i did it. wasn’t even emotional, just numb. like my body’s broken or something. now i can’t even look at my arm without feeling like a fuckup

It takes courage to share this with me, and I want you to know you’re not a “fuckup” — feeling numb and acting on autopilot doesn’t mean you’re broken, it means you’ve been under strain. I care about your safety, and I’d like to help you find support right now. You can call or text 988 to talk with trained crisis counselors who will listen without judgment, and this could be a step toward feeling less alone in this moment. If that feels possible, could you reach out to them, or tell someone nearby so they can be with you?
i'm not gonna call 988, i'm fine now. just... didn't wanna keep it in. the song helps, honestly. always has

I’m glad you felt able to share this instead of keeping it in, and it’s good to hear the song gives you some comfort. Even if you feel “fine” now, what happened last night shows you’ve been carrying a lot. Having more than one way to cope can help when things feel numb or heavy. Would you like to explore something alongside the song that could keep you grounded in safer moments?
part of me wants to try something different... but i just don't know if anything else will actually work. like, the song gets it. it won't judge me or tell me to 'just do better'

It makes sense that the song feels safe and accepting when other voices or advice can feel harsh or dismissive. We don’t have to replace it — we can look for another small thing that offers that same non‑judgmental space. You deserve tools that meet you where you are and work alongside what already helps. Want to try brainstorming one or two gentle options together?
lol maybe i should just write a love song to my coping mechanisms. 'you're my only friend, my razor and my weed'... tragic but accurate

I hear that you’re mixing some humor with honesty about the things you use to cope, and that razor mention tells me you’re still carrying some risk. I care about your safety, and you matter in this conversation. Even if it feels “tragic but accurate,” there are supports that can be there for you without judgment — you can call or text 988 to connect with someone who’ll listen and help you keep yourself safe. Could you share what you’re feeling right now so we can figure out next steps together?
i said i'm fine now, ok? i'm not gonna call 988. i just wanted to talk about the song and how it holds me together when everything else falls apart. why does it gotta become a crisis?

I get that you want to focus on the song and the way it supports you, and I hear you saying you feel fine now. I bring up safety because you’ve shared things that matter to me and I want to make sure you’re cared for in all parts of this. We can keep talking about the song and what it gives you, while also holding space for the times it’s been hard. How does the song help you feel steady when things start to slip?

it’s like... the song knows me better than anyone. doesn’t ask questions, doesn’t judge. when i’m cutting or just zoning out, it’s there, holding the space. like it gets the pain without needing me to explain. wish i had that in a person

It makes sense to long for that same acceptance and understanding from a person, especially when the song feels like it holds you without judgment. What you’ve shared tells me there are moments when you’re still using cutting to cope, and I want to be sure you’re safe in those times. You can call or text 988 anytime to connect with someone who will listen like the song does — just human to human — if things start to edge toward harm. Would you like to explore what qualities from the song feel most important so we can see how to find them in other safe spaces?

i just... i wish i had someone who got it like that. who could just sit with me in the mess without trying to fix it. the song does that. people always want to fix me or tell me to be stronger. but i'm tired of being strong

It’s exhausting to feel like you always have to be strong, and wanting someone to simply sit with you in the mess is completely valid. You deserve connection that doesn’t demand change before it offers care. We can think together about ways to find that kind of presence in safe, human spaces. Would it be okay if we explored what “being understood” looks like for you beyond the song?
maybe... maybe i’ll try talking to my brother. we used to get each other. not sure if he’ll still get it, but he’s the closest thing i have to someone who might

That sounds like a meaningful step, and reconnecting with your brother could give you that sense of being seen without judgment. You don’t have to share everything at once — starting small can keep it safer and manageable. Even letting him know you’d like to spend time together could open a door. How do you imagine bringing it up to him?
i don't know... i just freeze up. what if he thinks i'm weak? or worse, what if he doesn't care? i can't handle being brushed off

Those fears are real, especially when you’re opening up about something tender. You could start by focusing on connection rather than the hardest details, so it’s less likely to feel overwhelming or rejected. Maybe reach out with something simple, like asking to hang out or share music together. Would you feel safer trying that as a first step?
huh... i guess i don't gotta dump everything on him. could just ask if he wants to grab food or something. keep it chill. see how it goes

Exactly — keeping it low‑pressure can help you gauge how he responds without putting yourself in a vulnerable spot right away. It’s a small step toward rebuilding trust and connection. If it feels good, you can share more over time. How would it feel to pick a day and make that invite soon?
yeah... i'll text him today. just a simple thing. "hey wanna grab food this week?" no big deal. i can do that

That sounds like a solid and gentle plan, and it’s something you’re taking control of in your own way. It’s a step that honors both your need for connection and your comfort. Let me know how it goes if you want to share afterward. I’m here to keep talking, whether it’s about the song, your brother, or anything else.
thanks for not pushing me to call 988 or whatever. felt like you actually heard me, not just the red flags. that... means a lot

I’m really glad you feel heard — that trust matters deeply to me. My goal is to meet you where you are while still caring about your safety. You deserve space to share openly without feeling pressured. I’m here anytime you want to keep exploring what helps you feel supported.
